key_insight: Synthetic biomedical data can accelerate model development, but good results in simulation do not automatically translate to good results in the real world. The paper highlights the simulation-to-reality gap as the central barrier and argues for more reliable ways to judge synthetic data usefulness.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of using synthetic datasets to build biomedical machine learning models when performance in virtual experiments fails to predict real-world performance. It focuses on the mismatch between simulated and actual biological data.
method: Discusses the role of synthetic data in biomedical ML and where it helps most.
Analyzes the simulation-to-reality gap that limits transfer from synthetic training/testing to real clinical settings.
Frames practical considerations for evaluating whether synthetic datasets produce trustworthy downstream performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work is a reminder that synthetic data should be validated against real-world outcomes, not just simulation metrics. It helps guide better dataset design, evaluation, and deployment decisions in biomedical AI.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing synthetic data generation, model training, and real-world deployment with a highlighted gap between simulation and reality.
A side-by-side comparison chart of performance on synthetic versus real biomedical data.
An icon-based workflow illustrating data generation, validation, and clinical translation.
A gap or bridge graphic visualizing the simulation-to-reality mismatch.
paper_title: From virtual experiments to biomedical insight with synthetic data
paper_authors: Margarida Victoriano, Milena Pavlović, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Hélder P. Oliveira, Artur Rocha
